cohort: 160 IVF-conceived neonates and 160 naturally conceived neonates, all born at term (37-39 weeks and 6 days) via cesarean section and with normal birth weight (2500-4000g)
finding: Neonates conceived through IVF had significantly higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure (SPAP) compared to naturally conceived neonates, suggesting a potential link between IVF and pulmonary hypertension.
mod_finding: The study exclusively examined cesarean newborns, both those conceived through IVF and those naturally conceived, to assess pulmonary arterial pressure.
